metadata.title: Continuous Delivery Assessment
metadata.intro:
About Continuous Delivery

Continuous Delivery (CD) is the ability to get changes of all types—including new features, configuration changes, bug fixes and experiments—into production, or into the hands of users, safely and quickly in a sustainable way.

This Continuous Delivery Assessment provides a framework for reflection and for identifying opportunities for improvement in your delivery process. By evaluating key aspects of your pipeline, we aim to identify bottlenecks and areas for optimization.

This assessment evaluates four key categories: Deployability, Feedback, Automation, and Agility.
metadata.feedback_message: Thank you for using our Continuous Delivery assessment! We hope you found it valuable.  While you're here, we'd love to hear your thoughts and feedback to help us improve this tool.

questions.text: You just found a bug in production, when will it be fixed in production?

options.description: Next week or beyond
Some time this week
Today

questions.text: How often are deployments blocked by an issue with builds or tests

options.description: Most weeks
A couple of times a month
Rarely

questions.text: How long is a deployment typically blocked when there's an issue with builds or tests

options.description: More than a day
More than an hour but less than a day
Less than an hour

questions.text: The build just failed, when does it get fixed?

options.description: When we prepare the next software version
Once we finish whatever we're working on
We pause everything and fix it straight away

questions.text: A bug has been found in a pre-production environment that would stop the software version going live, when does it get fixed?

options.description: When we prepare the next software version
Once we finish whatever we're working on
We pause everything and fix it straight away

questions.text: How many teams outside of development need to sign off a production deployment, for example testing is done by an external team or release management is a separate department?

options.description: More than two
One or two
None

questions.text: Can developers and testers deploy to a pre-live environment on demand

options.description: No, they need to obtain sigh-off, or raise a ticket, or ask someone else to trigger the deployment
Yes, if they co-ordinate with others to avoid deploying when someone is using an environment
Yes, they can deploy to a pre-live environment on demand without co-ordination or approval

questions.text: How often does you code get merged into the main branch?

options.description: Less often than every day
Each day
Every hour or two

questions.text: How often do other team members merge into the main branch?

options.description: Less often than every day
Each day
Every hour or two

questions.text: How long after a code commit do you get the results of the build and tests?

options.description: Longer than 20 minutes
Between 5 and 20 minutes
In about 5 minutes or less

questions.text: How do changes progress through environments

options.description: We deploy manually to all environments
We have automated deployments to pre-production environments but a different process is used to deploy to production
The exact same automated/push-button process deploys to all environments

questions.text: If a bug was reported in a specific version of your software

options.description: We would have to build and deploy that version of the software to test it
We could manually re-deploy that version from a store of software versions
Our automated push-button process could deploy that version to a test environment

questions.text: How much of your deployment pipeline, from code commit to running in production, depends on a manual stage gate? For example, manual testing, security, packaging, moving files around, configuration, etc.

options.description: The deployment pipeline is mostly manual
The deployment pipeline has some automation and some manual stages
We aggressively automate all stages of the deployment pipeline unless we can find no economic way to do it

questions.text: Do you have any stages that happen outside of the deployment pipeline, for example security tests running quarterly rather than for every release?

options.description: Many stages are out of band, such as security testing, capacity testing, or vulnerability scanning.
Most stages are done as part of the deployment pipeline
All checks happen as part of the deployment pipeline

questions.text: Build artifacts

options.description: The build step creates a new package each time the software is promoted to the next environment
The package is built once and the same package is used each time the software is promoted to the next environment

questions.text: Deployment process

options.description: The deployment process might be updated between environments, for example if we find a step was missing or a config value had changed
The deployment process is versioned alongside the package to keep it the same on all environments, changes would mean starting from the first environment again

questions.text: After you deploy to an environment

options.description: We depend on testers to check it's working
An automated test or script checks the application is running and its dependencies are available

questions.text: Environment similarity

options.description: Our pre-production environments have significant differences to the production environment
Our pre-production environments are mostly the same as production, with non-critical differences, like not needing the application firewall or load-balancers we use in production
Our pre-productions are very similar to the production environment

questions.text: Infrastructure changes

options.description: All changes are manual and we're not certain environments are kept in sync when changes are made
All changes are manual but we progress changes through our environments like we do code changes to keep them in sync and test our changes
Our environments use version-controlled configuration that keeps them identical, though we may use smaller instances for pre-production

questions.text: New features

options.description: New features appear when we deploy
We use coding techniques that keep new features hidden until they're ready (like keystoning)
We use feature flags to control visibility of new features

questions.text: New features

options.description: All users get a new feature at the same time
Users on a specific instance get new features before our general users (for example, a beta instance)
We can expose a new feature to specific users or groups of users

questions.text: How can you check what version of each component is deployed to each environment?

options.description: We track this manually, for example on a whiteboard or wiki page
This is tracked automatically and we can find a version by looking up that component's deployment information
This is tracked automatically and we can see this information for a set of related components all on a single dashboard

questions.text: How do you know a deployment is taking place?

options.description: We signal this manually, for example in our internal chat tools or by email
This is tracked automatically and we can see running deployments by looking up that component's deployment information
This is tracked automatically and we can see running deployments for a set of related components all on a single dashboard
